propositions.text: Claimant is a DRC citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b).
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and paragraphs 97(1)(a) and (b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

propositions.text: Minister requests claimant's exclusion under IRPA section 98 and UN Convention articles 1F(a) and (c).
propositions.quote: The Minister of Public Safety (the Minister) is intervening in this claim and is requesting that the claimant be excluded from the benefit of sections 96 and 97, pursuant to section 98 of the IRPA, under articles 1F(a) and (c)1 of the United Nations Convention relating to the Status of Refugees (the Convention).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a DRC citizen, seeks refugee protection; the Minister requests exclusion under IRPA section 98 and UN Convention articles 1F(a) and (c).

propositions.text: Claimant fears for life due to political activities with MLC, detained in 2007, fled to US, then entered Canada in 2008 claiming refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The claimant fears for his life because of his political activities with the Mouvement pour la Libération du Congo (MLC) ... He was released under pressure ... and managed to flee the DRC ... He entered Canada on January 2, 2008, and claimed refugee protection that day.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fears for his life due to MLC political activities, was detained, fled to US, then entered Canada in 2008 claiming refugee protection.

propositions.text: Claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction through submitted identity documents.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction through the identity documents submitted on the record.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction through submitted documents.

propositions.text: Minister alleges serious reasons to consider claimant committed or was complicit in crimes against peace, war crimes, crimes against humanity, or acts contrary to UN purposes and principles.
propositions.quote: The Minister is requesting the claimant's exclusion because, in his opinion, there are serious reasons for considering that he has committed or was complicit in crimes against peace, war crimes or crimes against humanity, or that he has been guilty of acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations.

propositions.text: Section 98 IRPA excludes persons referred to in article 1F of the Convention from refugee status.
propositions.quote: According to section 98 of the IRPA, a person referred to in article 1F of the Convention is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The Minister alleges claimant's exclusion due to serious reasons under article 1F; section 98 IRPA excludes such persons from refugee status.

propositions.text: Parties agreed member will decide exclusion first; if no exclusion, hearing on claim will reconvene.
propositions.quote: It was agreed at the hearing that I will render a decision on the claimant's exclusion and that if I do not exclude him, I will reconvene the parties to hear his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The member will decide exclusion first; if claimant not excluded, hearing on claim will reconvene.

propositions.text: Section 98 IRPA excludes persons under articles 1F(a) or (c) of the Convention from refugee status.
propositions.quote: Section 98 of the IRPA states that a person referred to in articles 1F(a) or (c) of the Convention is not a refugee; that is, any person: with respect to whom there are serious reasons for considering that: (a) He has committed a crime against peace, a war crime, or a crime against humanity... (c) He has been guilty of acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations. is not a refugee.

propositions.text: Minister bears burden of proof on exclusion, lower than balance of probabilities; exclusion clauses interpreted restrictively due to serious consequences.
propositions.quote: The burden of proof imposed in such a case rests on the Minister and, according to the case law, is lower than the balance of probabilities. That said, given the serious consequences of an exclusion on a claim for protection, the exclusion clauses must be interpreted restrictively.

paragraphs.summary: Section 98 IRPA excludes persons under articles 1F(a) or (c); Minister bears burden of proof, lower than balance of probabilities; exclusion clauses interpreted restrictively.

propositions.text: Must determine if MLC committed acts in article 1F during claimant's membership period.
propositions.quote: I must first determine whether the MLC committed, during the time the claimant was a member (I will return to this question), the acts mentioned in article 1F.

propositions.text: Will refer to non-exhaustive excerpts from Minister's evidence.
propositions.quote: I will now refer to some non-exhaustive excerpts from the evidence submitted by the Minister.

paragraphs.summary: Must determine if MLC committed article 1F acts during claimant's membership; will refer to Minister's evidence excerpts.

propositions.text: Minister cited many excerpts from international human rights organizations; these are reliable sources.
propositions.quote: During the hearing, the Minister's representative cited a large number of excerpts from the documentary evidence issued by international human rights organizations... In my opinion, these are reliable sources.

paragraphs.summary: Minister cited many excerpts from international human rights organizations, which the court finds reliable.

propositions.text: MLC is a political and military movement led by Jean-Pierre Bemba, founded June 1999 to topple dictatorial government by political and armed means.
propositions.quote: The MLC is a political and military movement led by Jean-Pierre Bemba and founded in June 1999 with the acknowledged goal of toppling the dictatorial government through political means and armed battle.

paragraphs.summary: MLC is a political and military movement led by Bemba, founded in 1999 to topple the dictatorial government.

propositions.text: From formation to end 2003, MLC members committed murder, rape, arbitrary detention, disappearances, killings, torture, fires, pillaging, massacres on large scale targeting thousands.
propositions.quote: MLC members... have engaged in murder; rape as a tool of warfare... arrests and arbitrary detentions; disappearances and arbitrary killings of civilians; torture; fires; pillaging; and massacres... thousands and thousands of innocent victims were targeted.

paragraphs.summary: From formation to 2003, MLC committed widespread murder, rape, arbitrary detention, disappearances, torture, pillaging, massacres targeting thousands.

propositions.text: Evidence reports cannibalism by ALC soldiers with MLC leaders' knowledge; ALC recruited thousands of child soldiers subjected to horrors including forced fighting, rape, cannibalism, sex slavery.
propositions.quote: The evidence also reports incidences of cannibalism by soldiers of the Armée de Libération du Congo (ALC)... The evidence further reports that the ALC recruited thousands of child soldiers... forced to fight and often kill their own families, forced to engage in cannibalism, raped, and used as sex slaves.

propositions.text: ALC is integral part of MLC as stated in MLC's statutes.
propositions.quote: It is important to point out that the ALC is an integral part of the MLC, which is clearly stated in the MLC's statutes.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows ALC soldiers committed cannibalism and recruited child soldiers; ALC is integral to MLC per its statutes.

propositions.text: MLC responsible for serious and systematic human rights violations from 1999 to late 2003 as political and military movement.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the MLC was responsible for serious and systematic human rights violations during the time that it was a political and military movement, that is, from 1999 to late 2003.

paragraphs.summary: MLC was responsible for serious and systematic human rights violations from 1999 to late 2003.

propositions.text: Must determine if MLC's acts are crimes against peace, war crimes, crimes against humanity, or acts contrary to UN purposes and principles.
propositions.quote: I must now determine whether the acts that I just mentioned are crimes against peace, war crimes, crimes against humanity, or acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations.

paragraphs.summary: Must determine if MLC's acts qualify as crimes against peace, war crimes, crimes against humanity, or acts contrary to UN purposes.

propositions.text: Definition of crimes against humanity includes murder, extermination, enslavement, deportation, inhumane acts, persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds.
propositions.quote: The definition of "crimes against humanity" set out in the London Agreement reads: Article 6 ... Crimes against humanity: namely, murder, extermination, enslavement, deportation, and other inhumane acts committed against any civilian population, before or during the war; or persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds ...

paragraphs.summary: London Agreement defines crimes against humanity as murder, extermination, enslavement, deportation, inhumane acts, persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds.

propositions.text: Crimes against humanity must generally be committed in widespread, systematic fashion.
propositions.quote: Other cases adopt a similar definition. Sivakumar adds an important dimension: Crimes against humanity must generally be committed in a widespread, systematic fashion;

paragraphs.summary: Crimes against humanity must generally be committed in widespread, systematic fashion.

propositions.text: Mugesera states four elements for crime against humanity: proscribed act committed with guilty mind; part of widespread/systematic attack; attack directed at civilians; perpetrator knew of attack and risk.
propositions.quote: Mugesera clearly states the conditions under which a criminal act may be considered a crime against humanity: ... four elements ...

paragraphs.summary: Mugesera sets four elements for crimes against humanity: proscribed act, widespread/systematic attack, civilian target, perpetrator knowledge.

propositions.text: Evidence shows MLC from 2000 to 2003 systematically committed barbaric, inhumane acts and serious persecution widespread and directed at civilians.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the evidence mentioned previously clearly demonstrates that the MLC, from 2000 to 2003, systematically committed a large number of barbaric and inhumane acts and serious acts of persecution and that this persecution was widespread and systematic and directed against the civilian population and the targeted groups.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows MLC from 2000-2003 systematically committed widespread barbaric, inhumane acts and serious persecution against civilians.

propositions.text: MLC committed crimes against humanity from 2000 to 2003; no need to consider other article 1F notions.
propositions.quote: I conclude that the MLC committed crimes against humanity during the above-mentioned period. In light of this conclusion, I do not need to visit the other notions set out in article 1F of the Convention.

paragraphs.summary: MLC committed crimes against humanity from 2000 to 2003; no need to consider other article 1F notions.

propositions.text: Must analyze if serious reasons exist to consider claimant complicit in crimes against humanity as actor or accomplice, since evidence does not show claimant committed acts himself.
propositions.quote: I will now analyze whether, in that context, there are serious reasons for considering that the claimant was complicit in crimes against humanity, either as an actor or as an accomplice, given that the evidence does not support a conclusion that the claimant himself committed the acts mentioned in the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Must analyze if serious reasons exist to consider claimant complicit in crimes against humanity, as evidence does not show claimant committed acts himself.

propositions.text: Determining when claimant was MLC member is key issue before analyzing complicity.
propositions.quote: Before analyzing whether the claimant was complicit, it is important to determine when he was a member of the MLC. This fact is one of the key issues in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Determining when claimant was MLC member is key issue before analyzing complicity.

propositions.text: Claimant denied MLC membership during crimes, said he joined in 2004, was briefly in a committee in 2002, not politically active until 2004
propositions.quote: the claimant denied that he was member of the MLC during the period that this movement committed all of the crimes mentioned. At the beginning of his testimony at the hearing, he alleged that he only joined the MLC in 2004. He testified that before then, in 2002, he was briefly a member of a XXXXX committee whose goal was to XXXXX XXXXX. He explained that as an XXXXX XXXXX, he wanted to ensure that he enjoyed certain benefits as soon as the MLC arrived, such as obtaining XXXXX XXXXX. He also testified that after a few months, this XXXXX XXXXX committee XXXXX. The claimant alleged that he was not involved in any political activities until XXXXX 2004, when he officially joined the MLC.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant denied MLC membership during crimes, alleging he joined in 2004 and was briefly in a committee in 2002 before political activity.

propositions.text: Claimant's hearing allegations contradict his refugee claim form stating MLC membership from 2000 without cessation
propositions.quote: These allegations are directly contrary to the fact that in the form that he completed when he initially claimed refugee protection,18 he indicated that he became a member of the MLC's XXXXX XXXXX 2000; he did not indicate that he had ceased being a member.

propositions.text: Claimant corrected testimony to say he joined committee in 2000, not 2002, and terms 'XXXXX committee' and 'XXXXX' are same
propositions.quote: Confronted with these major contradictions, the claimant first corrected his testimony and stated that he did indeed join the XXXXX committee in 2000, not in 2002. As for the contradiction between a [translation] "XXXXX committee" and a [translation] "XXXXX," the claimant explained that these terms refer to the same organization.

paragraphs.summary: The court found claimant's hearing allegations contradict his refugee form; claimant corrected testimony to say he joined committee in 2000 and terms are same.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he did not indicate cessation or joining dates in form due to nature and space limits
propositions.quote: Finally, as for why he did not indicate in the form completed at the port of entry that he had ceased being a member of the "XXXXX committee XXXXX" in 2000 and that he did not join the MLC itself until 2004, but rather indicated that he became a member of the MLC in 2000 without interruption, the claimant testified that it is in his nature to explain everything and that there was not enough space in the form to write down every detail.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified he omitted cessation and joining details in form due to nature and space limits.

propositions.text: Claimant was warned in 2009 interview that MLC membership could be problematic due to human rights violations
propositions.quote: During the interview, which was recorded,19 the tribunal officer explained to the claimant that his membership in the MLC could be problematic, given the human rights violations that this movement has committed.

propositions.text: Claimant admitted in 2009 interview to being a contributing MLC member since 2000 after warning
propositions.quote: After this clearly worded warning, the claimant stated that he was indeed a member of the MLC. Asked since when, he stated that he has been [translation] "a contributing member since 2000."

paragraphs.summary: In 2009 interview, claimant was warned MLC membership was problematic and admitted being a contributing member since 2000.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant changed account, saying he meant 'XXXXX committee' not MLC at interview, but could not explain
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the claimant was confronted with the statements he made at the expedited interview. He changed his account and indicated that he had meant to say XXXXX committee when he said MLC. He was going to explain himself at the end of the interview, but found himself in the situation of being unable to explain.

paragraphs.summary: At hearing, claimant changed account, saying he meant committee not MLC at interview, but could not explain.

propositions.text: Claimant defined 'contributing member' as referring to committee, expecting to become MLC members when MLC arrived
propositions.quote: When asked at the hearing for his definition of "contributing member," the expression that he used at the expedited interview, the claimant testified that he was talking about the XXXXX committee, because the actions of that committee commanded success. He added, [translation] "It was clear that when the MLC came, we would become members of the MLC."

paragraphs.summary: Claimant defined 'contributing member' as committee member, expecting to become MLC members when MLC arrived.

propositions.text: Claimant tried to change incriminating testimony at hearing but told truth spontaneously at port of entry and interview
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the claimant tried at the hearing to change testimony that he now realizes is highly incriminating, given the Minister's intervention submitted in March 2009, and that at the port of entry in January 2008 and at his expedited interview in January 2009, he spontaneously told the truth about his membership in the MLC.

propositions.text: Martineau J. in Mohacsi stated claimant's first story is usually most genuine and to be most believed
propositions.quote: In the words of Martineau J. in Mohacsi:20 Fourth, a claimant's first story is usually the most genuine and, therefore, the one to be most believed.

paragraphs.summary: Court found claimant tried to change incriminating testimony but first story is usually most genuine, per Martineau J.

propositions.text: Martineau J. in Nava Chavez said no reason to doubt principal applicant's statements to immigration officer, who is educated and can explain reasons
propositions.quote: Even more relevant is the statement of Martineau, J. in Nava Chavez:21 There is no reason here to doubt the truth and the accuracy of the statements made by the principal applicant to the immigration officer. Moreover, I note that the principal applicant is an educated man and a lawyer. It is therefore reasonable to expect him to be able to give the immigration officer and the Board a clear explanation of his reasons for leaving Mexico.

propositions.text: No real prejudice caused by interpreter mistakes at hearing or initial interview
propositions.quote: Finally, this is not a case in which the evidence on record shows that real prejudice was caused to the claimant for refugee protection because of flagrant mistakes in interpretation made by an interpreter at the hearing or at the initial interview with the immigration officer.

paragraphs.summary: Martineau J. in Nava Chavez said no reason to doubt applicant's statements to immigration officer and no interpreter prejudice.

propositions.text: Claimant is educated, speaks French, should know importance of statements to immigration authorities
propositions.quote: In this case, the claimant is also a XXXXX and speaks excellent French; he reasonably should know the importance of the statements that he was making to the Canadian immigration authorities, whom he was asking to protect him.

propositions.text: Court believes claimant has been MLC member since 2000 until leaving DRC
propositions.quote: Consequently, I believe that the claimant has been a member of the MLC since 2000 and that he did not cease being a member until he left the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: Court found claimant educated, knew importance of statements, and believes claimant was MLC member from 2000 until leaving DRC.

propositions.text: Complicity in crimes against humanity requires shared purpose and knowing participation; mens rea is critical
propositions.quote: The consistent case law on this matter indicates that complicity in crimes against humanity implies a shared common purpose and personal and knowing participation in the acts of which the organization is guilty. More specifically, an individual who is part of such an organization, who does not take measures to prevent the acts committed by the organization if it is possible to do so, and who does not dissociate himself or herself from the organization at the first possible opportunity, but who on the contrary actively supports the organization, demonstrates a shared common purpose. Mens rea is therefore a critical element when assessing complicity.

paragraphs.summary: Court states complicity requires shared purpose, knowing participation, and mens rea is critical.

propositions.text: Mosley J. said complicity requires personal and knowing participation and shared common purpose; membership sufficient if organization has brutal purpose
propositions.quote: I cannot express myself better than Mosley J., when he addressed complicity in the context of exclusion: The law makes it clear that in order to be complicit in the commission of an international offence an individual's participation must be personal and knowing. Complicity in such an offence rests on a shared common purpose: Gutierrez, above at para. 22, citing Penate, above at para. 4 This has been described as the mens rea requirement of the exclusion clause: Cardenas v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1994] F.C.J. No. 139 at para. 12 (T.D.) (QL) [Cardenas]. In the context of assessing complicity by way of involvement with an organization, the first step is to look at the purpose of the organization in question. Where the "main objective of the organization is achieved by crimes against humanity or is directed towards a limited and brutal purpose, membership is generally sufficient to establish complicity": Pushpanathan v. Canada, at para. 41. Unless the organization at issue is found to have a limited, brutal purpose however, mere membership in a group responsible for international crimes is not enough: Sivakumar, above at para. 13. 22

paragraphs.summary: Mosley J. said complicity requires personal knowing participation and shared purpose; membership suffices if organization has brutal purpose.

propositions.text: Whether MLC from 2000 was an organization directed toward a limited and brutal purpose
propositions.quote: Therefore, I must determine whether the MLC, at the time the claimant was a member, that is, starting in 2000, can be described as an organization directed toward a limited and brutal purpose.

propositions.text: Organization achieving political or social ends by any means is presumed to imply complicity by membership
propositions.quote: The case law indicates that an organization whose very existence "is premised on achieving political or social ends by any means deemed necessary"23 is open to a presumption that mere membership in that organization implies complicity, without necessarily linking the claimant's complicity to a particular crime committed by the organization.

propositions.text: Ramirez says membership in organization with limited brutal purpose may involve personal participation in persecutorial acts
propositions.quote: The Federal Court in Ramirez,24 a key case in this matter, states as follows: It seems apparent, however, that where an organization is principally directed to a limited, brutal purpose, such as a secret police activity, mere membership may by necessity involve personal and knowing participation in persecutorial acts.

paragraphs.summary: Court must decide if MLC from 2000 had brutal purpose; case law presumes complicity by membership in such groups.

propositions.text: Federal Court in Pushpanathan ruled on when a political organization is directed toward limited and brutal purposes
propositions.quote: The Federal Court was called upon in Pushpanathan25 to rule on what determines that an organization that otherwise pursues political objectives is directed toward limited and brutal purposes.

propositions.text: If political objectives cannot be separated from militaristic activities, organization may be found to have limited brutal purpose
propositions.quote: ...where there is no evidence that political objectives can be separated from militaristic activities, an organization could still be found to have a limited, brutal purpose.

propositions.text: If main objective is achieved by crimes against humanity or limited brutal purpose, membership suffices to establish complicity
propositions.quote: If the main objective of the organization is achieved by crimes against humanity or is directed towards a limited and brutal purpose, membership is generally sufficient to establish complicity.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court in Pushpanathan ruled that if political objectives are inseparable from militaristic activities, membership suffices to establish complicity in crimes against humanity.

propositions.text: From 2000 to 2003, MLC's main objective was to topple Kabila's dictatorship and assume power, as per its statutes
propositions.quote: My analysis of the documentary evidence entered on this record leads me to conclude that, from 2000 to the end of 2003, the years during which the claimant was a member, the MLC's main objective was to topple Kabila's dictatorship and assume power; this objective is even indicated in the MLC's statutes, as I mentioned previously.

propositions.text: Claimant was member of political branch, but MLC hoped to achieve objectives primarily through armed branch, which was not dissociated
propositions.quote: although the claimant was a member of the movement's political branch and not its armed branch, being a member of the "legal college", it is clear that the MLC hoped to achieve its objectives primarily through its armed branch, which was not dissociated from it; the MLC's statutes once again are clear on this, and the documentary evidence confirms this.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds MLC aimed to topple Kabila from 2000-2003, claimant was in political branch but MLC relied on armed branch to achieve goals.

propositions.text: MLC used all means necessary including arbitrary arrest, murder, rape, summary execution, cannibalism, massacre, torture, pillaging, fires, child soldiers
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the evidence establishes that the MLC used all means deemed necessary to achieve its objectives, means that I mentioned earlier: arbitrary arrest, murder, rape, summary execution, cannibalism, massacre, systematic torture, pillaging, fires and the use of child soldiers.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds MLC used brutal means including murder, rape, torture, and child soldiers to achieve objectives.

propositions.text: MLC was directed to a limited and brutal purpose during claimant's membership years
propositions.quote: The evidence clearly shows that the MLC, in the years the claimant was a member, was an organization directed to a limited and brutal purpose.

propositions.text: Presumed claimant has mens rea required for complicity in crimes against humanity committed by MLC
propositions.quote: In this case, it is presumed that the claimant has the mental capacity required, the mens rea necessary for a conclusion of complicity.

propositions.text: Claimant is presumed complicit in crimes against humanity committed by MLC from 2000 to 2003
propositions.quote: The claimant is therefore presumed to be complicit in the crimes against humanity committed by the MLC from 2000 to the end of 2003.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds MLC had limited brutal purpose and presumes claimant complicit in crimes against humanity from 2000-2003.

propositions.text: Presumption of complicity is rebuttable
propositions.quote: This presumption is rebuttable.

propositions.text: To determine rebuttal, court considers Ryivuze criteria for complicity: six factors listed by Federal Court
propositions.quote: To determine whether the claimant could reverse it, I considered the criteria set out in Ryivuze28 to determine complicity: Determining whether or not Mr. Ryivuze was complicit in the crimes committed by the government of Burundi is essentially a question of fact which requires an assessment of his personal situation. (Sivakumar, supra, at paragraph 2) On this point, the Federal Court has listed six factors which must be considered to determine whether or not an individual is complicit in crimes against humanity: (1) the nature of the organization; (2) the method of recruitment; (3) position/rank in the organization; (4) knowledge of the organization's atrocities; (5) the length of time in the organization; and (6) the opportunity to leave the organization. Nature of the organization

paragraphs.summary: The court states presumption of complicity is rebuttable and applies Ryivuze six-factor test to assess claimant's complicity.

propositions.text: MLC is an organization directed to a limited and brutal purpose
propositions.quote: I have already determined that the nature of the MLC is that of an organization directed to a limited and brutal purpose.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds MLC is directed to a limited and brutal purpose.

propositions.text: Claimant joined MLC voluntarily, seeking political advancement and espousing its political convictions
propositions.quote: It is clear that the claimant joined the MLC voluntarily. In fact, he testified that he wanted to better position himself on the political ladder and become a XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX. He also testified, [translation] "I espoused their political convictions; I was hoping for a new political era."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant voluntarily joined MLC to advance politically and shared its political beliefs.

propositions.text: Claimant held a XXXXX or at least XXXXX as member of XXXXX, not a subordinate unaware of organization's direction
propositions.quote: The claimant held a XXXXX, or at the very least XXXXX, as a member of the XXXXX. He was not a subordinate who did not know the direction his organization was taking.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant held a significant position in the organization and was aware of its direction.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony about his knowledge of MLC atrocities was not credible.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony regarding his knowledge of the atrocities committed by the MLC was not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's testimony about his knowledge of MLC atrocities not credible.

propositions.text: The claimant initially said he knew no details about the MLC armed branch, but documentary evidence shows violations were well-known and publicized.
propositions.quote: He initially testified that he did not know any details concerning the armed branch of the MLC. However, the documentary evidence indicates that the violations committed by the ALC were well-known and highly publicized.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant initially denied knowledge but evidence shows MLC violations were well-known and publicized.

propositions.text: The claimant minimized ongoing MLC fighting after the 2001 ceasefire despite evidence to the contrary.
propositions.quote: When confronted with the evidence cited previously, which mentions that, on the contrary, the MLC continued to fight at the end of 2001 in the country's eastern areas, the claimant answered, "It was no longer a war with the MLC. The conflict was between the forces that were there."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant minimized MLC fighting after the ceasefire despite contrary evidence.

propositions.text: The claimant admitted having some information on MLC violations but claimed limited details and denied knowledge of systematic rape and murder of civilians.
propositions.quote: After several questions and confrontations, the claimant finally testified that between 2000 and 2004, he "did indeed have information on this," speaking about the violations committed by the MLC. ... he answered that he had not [heard of systematic rape and murder].

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant admitted some knowledge but denied details of systematic abuses by the MLC.

propositions.text: The claimant dismissed government reports on MLC abuses as political brainwashing and did not verify their truth due to work commitments.
propositions.quote: He did not try to verify whether the reports were true because, according to his testimony, he was very busy with his work at the XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant dismissed abuse reports as brainwashing and did not verify them due to work.

propositions.text: The claimant acknowledged hearing about clashes and possible massacres but minimized their significance and did not seek details.
propositions.quote: Later in his testimony, the claimant tried to minimize the situation. He stated, "That depends on the meaning you give to the word massacre. When I hear that someone died, am I going to try to find out if it was a massacre?"

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant minimized massacres and did not investigate their details.

propositions.text: The claimant initially believed reports of MLC cannibalism but later doubted them, despite admissions by MLC leader Bemba.
propositions.quote: At first I believed it, but then I doubted this information. It is beyond human understanding that there was cannibalism in the Congo.

propositions.text: The claimant's attempts to minimize abuses while denying membership are contradictory and implausible given the gravity of MLC crimes.
propositions.quote: I do not accept these attempts at justification. First, the claimant's attempts to minimize the abuses committed by the MLC yet at the same time claim that he was not a member are contradictory. In addition, it is implausible that the claimant was not aware of the gravity and the systematic and systemic nature of the crimes committed by the MLC.

propositions.text: If a person lives and works where people disappear and are tortured, it is unbelievable they would not know what is happening (Shakarabi).
propositions.quote: If, as in the present case, an individual lives and works in a country where persons around him are disappearing and where one hears of persons arrested and tortured, it appears to me to be totally unbelievable that one would not have knowledge of what is taking place.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's denial and minimization contradictory and cites Shakarabi that one cannot be unaware of such crimes.

propositions.text: The claimant said child soldier recruitment was possible but only in 1998-1999 by former regime soldiers, denying knowledge of 2002 recruitment.
propositions.quote: At a given point during the hearing, the claimant stopped his denials and admitted that the MLC was an armed movement before 2004 and that he knew it, and that he knew that even the political branch supported the armed conflict, in accordance with the movement's statutes.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant admitted MLC was armed before 2004 but denied knowledge of child soldier recruitment after 1999.

propositions.text: The claimant admitted the MLC was armed before 2004 and that he knew the political branch supported armed conflict.
propositions.quote: At a given point during the hearing, the claimant stopped his denials and admitted that the MLC was an armed movement before 2004 and that he knew it, and that he knew that even the political branch supported the armed conflict, in accordance with the movement's statutes.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant admitted MLC was armed before 2004 and he knew political support for conflict.

propositions.text: The court does not believe the claimant's claim he joined the MLC only in 2004; he was active during abuses.
propositions.quote: I have already explained why I do not believe the claimant when he alleges that he did not join the MLC until 2004. I believe that he was an active member of the MLC during the entire period that the movement was committing the abuses.

paragraphs.summary: The court disbelieves the claimant's claim of joining MLC in 2004 and finds he was active during abuses.

propositions.text: The claimant voluntarily remained with an organization he knew committed serious human rights violations.
propositions.quote: I conclude that the claimant voluntarily remained with an organization that he knew was guilty of serious human rights violations.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant voluntarily stayed with an organization committing serious human rights violations.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony showed nonchalance and lack of empathy for victims, minimizing serious crimes as normal war consequences.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony when confronted with the atrocities committed by the MLC was nonchalant and completely lacking in empathy for the thousands of victims. ... massacres of civilians; the systematic rape of women, girls and young girls; and the recruitment of child soldiers are not the collateral damage of a war.

propositions.text: The claimant's speech reflects an active MLC member who knew abuses but chose the MLC for political ambition aiming to become XXXXX XXXXX.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Minister that the claimant's speech is that of an active member of the MLC who knew what was going on but who, out of political ambition, chose the MLC, the only party that, in his opinion, could have assumed power from Kabila. He testified that his goal was to become a XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant showed nonchalance about atrocities and acted as an active MLC member with political ambition.

propositions.text: The claimant did not rebut the presumption of complicity in crimes against humanity by the MLC between 2000 and 2004.
propositions.quote: Consequently, I am of the opinion that the claimant did not rebut the presumption that he was complicit in crimes against humanity committed by the MLC between 2000 and 2004.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant failed to rebut presumption of complicity in MLC crimes from 2000 to 2004.

propositions.text: The claimant is described in article 1F(a) of the Convention as complicit in crimes against humanity.
propositions.quote: For the above-mentioned reasons, I determine that the claimant is described in article 1F(a) of the Convention, in that there are serious reasons to believe that he was complicit in crimes against humanity.

paragraphs.summary: The court determines the claimant is excluded under article 1F(a) for complicity in crimes against humanity.

propositions.text: Pursuant to section 98 of IRPA, the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Therefore, I determine, pursuant to section 98 of the IRPA, that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The court orders the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA section 98.
